title: Pope Leo visits Rome church where a vision of the Virgin Mary inspired a dramatic conversion
site_name: OSV News - We've got the Church covered
excerpt: Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass Nov. 27 in a church in Rome famous for a Marian apparition in 1842 and a dramatic conversion connected with the Miraculous Medal.
content:
Pope Leo XIV arrives in procession to celebrate Mass at the parish of Sant'Andrea delle Fratte in Rome on Nov. 27, 2026. (OSV News/Guglielmo Mangiapane, Reuters)

ROME (OSV News) — Pope Leo XIV celebrated Mass Nov. 27 in a church in Rome famous for a Marian apparition in 1842 and a dramatic conversion connected with the Miraculous Medal.

On the feast of Our Lady of the Miraculous Medal, the pope visited the Basilica of Sant’Andrea delle Fratte near the Spanish Steps, recalling that Pope Benedict XV, who led the Catholic Church from 1914-1922, once called the church “the Roman Lourdes.”

“I come as a pilgrim to invoke the help and intercession of the Virgin Mary at a difficult time in human history, marked by wars and unjust inequalities that undermine human dignity. I invite you to join me in this prayer,” Pope Leo said.

At the beginning of the Mass, Pope Leo stopped to pray in the side chapel where the apparition took place — the same chapel where St. Maximilian Kolbe decided to offer his first Mass on April 29, 1918, following his ordination to the priesthood in Rome.

In the chapel adorned with ex-voto silver hearts, votive offerings of gratitude for an answered prayers, Pope Leo asked the Virgin Mary to intercede in a special way for “the conversion of sinners, especially those who are dearest to us.”

The chapel is where the Virgin Mary appeared to Alphonse Ratisbonne, a French Freemason and an atheist of Jewish descent, on Jan. 20, 1842, leading to his profound conversion, which the Vatican recognized as a miracle following a canonical investigation. At the moment of the apparition, Ratisbonne was wearing a Miraculous Medal given to him by one of his Catholic friends in Rome earlier that month.

“Through devotion to this medal and the intercession of the Immaculate Virgin, many conversions are attributed to her. In this church, right at the foot of the Marian image, Alphonse Ratisbonne was touched by grace and fully embraced the Christian faith,” Pope Leo said in his homily.

“Brothers and sisters, Jesus calls us to conversion, to a change of perspective. Let us not view history as if there were nothing good left to be found in it, but let us learn to see it through his eyes, the eyes of the Risen One, which always bring true joy,” the pope added.

Vision of Mary ‘beautiful and full of mercy’

Ratisbonne described the vision which led to his conversion as “beautiful and full of mercy.”

“I looked over towards this chapel whence so much light shone, and above the altar was a living figure, tall, majestic, beautiful and full of mercy. It was the most holy Virgin Mary, resembling her figure on the Miraculous Medal. At this sight I fell on my knees right where I stood,” Ratisbonne said.

“In the presence of the Most Blessed Virgin, even though she did not speak a word to me, I understood the frightful situation I was in, my sins and the beauty of the Catholic faith.”

After his conversion, Ratisbonne went on to be ordained a Jesuit priest, but later left the order to move to Jerusalem in 1855, where he founded a convent for sisters in the Congregation of Our Lady of Sion, dedicated to witnessing God’s enduring love for the Jewish people.

In his homily, Pope Leo said it was no coincidence that the liturgy includes the Gospel account of the wedding feast at Cana for the memorial of Our Lady of the Miraculous Medal.

“Mary, in fact, appears there as the attentive Mother who notices what is lacking and entrusts it to her Son. This is precisely what this shrine has experienced over so many years of prayer,” he said.

Just as Jesus told the servants at the wedding in Cana to fill the jars with water, Pope Leo said, “Christ asks us to fill ourselves ‘to the brim,’ so that his abundance may find space in our obedience.”

“The Lord invites us to offer Him the little we have: a humanity tested by the loss of peace, young people struggling to build their future, families where dialogue has been lost, and the loneliness of so many in the cities. Jesus asks us to start from here, from people’s daily lives, in the certainty that He remains with us in this story and opens up a future within it,” he added.

Miraculous Medal inspired by the Marian apparition in Paris

The Miraculous Medal is a sacramental inspired by the Marian apparition to St. Catherine Labouré in Paris in 1830. The Virgin Mary appeared to her as the Immaculate Conception, standing on a globe, with light streaming from her hands and crushing a serpent underfoot.

“A voice said to me, ‘Have a medal struck after this model. All who wear it will receive great graces, especially if they wear it around the neck,'” St. Catherine recalled.

One side of the medal features a cross, the letter “M” and 12 stars, along with images of the Sacred Heart of Jesus and the Immaculate Heart of Mary. The other depicts Mary surrounded by the words: “O Mary, conceived without sin, pray for us who have recourse to you.”

St. Kolbe, who died at Auschwitz in 1941, called the Miraculous Medal a “heavenly weapon” for rescuing souls. He urged Catholics to give the medal to others and to pray for their conversation through Mary’s intercession.

“May your medal rest upon us and all our loved ones,” Pope Leo prayed before an image of Mary at the beginning of Mass. He asked her to bring healing to the sick, peace to families and to strengthen everyone to witness to the faith. “May it deliver us from every danger and bring comfort to those who suffer, consolation to those who weep, and light and strength to all,” he said.

Four more parish visits in Rome during Advent

The visit was the first of five parish visits Pope Leo has planned in Rome in the weeks leading up to Christmas. He will celebrate Mass at a different parish each Sunday during Advent, which begins Nov. 29 with a visit to San Carlo da Sezze, a parish known for accompanying young people and the poor in southern Rome.

He is scheduled to visit the Parish of St. Eligio Dec. 6, the parish of Santa Lucia Dec. 13, and the Parish of St. Robert Bellarmine, his patron saint, on Dec. 20, the fourth Sunday of Advent.

Pope Leo will return to the neighborhood of the Basilica of Sant’Andrea delle Fratte Dec. 8 to celebrate the solemnity of the Immaculate Conception with a traditional act of veneration near the Spanish Steps.

“We invoke Mary’s intercession, so that in this sanctuary the poor may find a listening ear, strangers a warm welcome, workers respect, and pilgrims a light of hope,” the pope said in the basilica.

“Every day, many of the faithful enter this church to offer a prayer and a plea for help to the Virgin, entrusting to her hands their sorrows, their thanksgiving, and their desires. We are certain that she receives everything with a mother’s heart. We entrust ourselves to her with confidence, asking for the gift to joyfully do each day what the Lord Jesus tells us.”
